metadata.title: On Some Sequences of Integers
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json lists this paper as 'On Certain Sets of Integers' by Roth (1953). The actual PDF/text is 'On Some Sequences of Integers' by Erdős and Turán (1936), J. London Math. Soc. 11. Extraction follows the actual PDF content.

nodes.name: A-sequence belonging to $N$
nodes.statement: A sequence of integers $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots \leq N$ that contains no three terms $a_i, a_j, a_k$ with $a_i - a_j = a_j - a_k$, i.e., no three-term arithmetic progression. Such a sequence is called an A-sequence belonging to $N$.
nodes.statement_clean: A set of positive integers up to $N$ with no three-term arithmetic progression.

nodes.name: Maximum function $r(N)$
nodes.statement: $r(N)$ denotes the number of elements of a maximum A-sequence belonging to $N$, i.e., the largest size of a subset of $\{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$ containing no three-term arithmetic progression.
nodes.statement_clean: $r(N)$ is the maximum size of a 3-AP-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.

nodes.name: Generalized maximum function $r_l(N)$
nodes.statement: $r_l(N)$ denotes the maximum number of integers $\leq N$ such that no $l$ of them form an arithmetic progression.
nodes.statement_clean: $r_l(N)$ generalizes $r(N)$ from 3-APs to $l$-term APs.

nodes.name: van der Waerden function $f(k, l)$
nodes.statement: $N = f(k, l)$ is the least integer such that any partition of $\{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$ into $l$ classes forces at least one class to contain a $k$-term arithmetic progression.
nodes.statement_clean: The classical van der Waerden number for $k$-APs and $l$ colors.

nodes.name: Reflection symmetry of A-sequences
nodes.statement: If $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_r$ is an A-sequence belonging to $N$, then $N+1-a_r < N+1-a_{r-1} < \cdots < N+1-a_1$ is also an A-sequence belonging to $N$.
nodes.statement_clean: The reflection $x \mapsto N+1-x$ preserves the A-sequence property.
assumptions: $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_r$ is an A-sequence belonging to $N$
conclusions: $\{N+1-a_i\}$ is also an A-sequence belonging to $N$

nodes.name: Translation invariance
nodes.statement: If $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_r$ is an A-sequence and $k < a_1$ is a non-negative integer, then $a_1 - k < a_2 - k < \cdots < a_r - k$ is also an A-sequence.
nodes.statement_clean: Translating an A-sequence by an integer preserves the A-sequence property.

nodes.name: Subadditivity of $r$
nodes.statement: For all positive integers $m, n$: $r(m+n) \leq r(m) + r(n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: $r$ is subadditive: $r(m+n) \leq r(m) + r(n)$.

nodes.name: Small-$N$ values of $r$
nodes.statement_clean: Explicit values and bounds for $r(N)$ at small $N$, used as base cases.

nodes.name: Theorem I (linear upper bound)
nodes.statement: For $N \geq 8$: $r(2N) \leq N$.
nodes.statement_clean: For $N \geq 8$, the maximum 3-AP-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,2N\}$ has at most $N$ elements.

nodes.name: Sharpness boundary for Theorem I
nodes.statement: The inequality $r(2N) \leq N$ holds for $N = 4, 5, 6$ but fails for $N = 7$ (since $r(14) = 8 > 7$).
nodes.statement_clean: Theorem I's bound is tight for some small $N$ but does not extend to $N = 7$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem I (induction)
nodes.statement: By induction: verify base cases $N = 4, 5, \ldots$ explicitly using symmetry (1) and translation (2); then for general $N$, apply subadditivity $r(2N) \leq r(2N-8) + r(8) \leq (N-3) + 4 = N+1$ together with the established cases $r(16), r(18), r(20), r(22)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Induction with base cases up to $N = 22$ and the subadditivity inequality.

nodes.name: Compute $r(8) = 4$
nodes.statement: If $r(8) = 5$, then by symmetry/translation we may assume $1$ and two integers $\leq 4$ lie in the sequence; the only candidates are $\{1,2,4\}$ or $\{1,3,4\}$, neither of which extends to size 5. Hence $r(8) \leq 4$, and $\{1,2,4,5\}$ achieves it, so $r(8) = 4$.

nodes.name: Compute $r(10) = 5$
nodes.statement: If $r(10) = 6$, then by $r(8) = 4$ and translation, $\{1, 2, 9, 10\}$ must occur; then $3, 5, 6, 8$ are forbidden, leaving only $\{1,2,4,7,9,10\}$ which contains $1, 4, 7$. So $r(10) \leq 5$; the sequence $\{1,2,4,9,10\}$ shows $r(10) = 5$.

nodes.name: Compute $r(12), r(13), r(14)$
nodes.statement: If $r(12) = 7$, the sequence must contain $\{1, 2, 4, 9, 11, 12\}$ with no room for additions, contradicting size 7; so $r(12) = 6$. The sequence $\{1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 11, 13, 14\}$ shows $r(14) = 8$ and $r(13) = 7$.

nodes.name: Apply subadditivity for $N = 16, 18, 20, 22$
nodes.statement: By $r(m+n) \leq r(m) + r(n)$ with the computed small values: $r(16) \leq 8$, $r(18) \leq 9$, $r(20) \leq 10$, $r(22) \leq 11$.

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: Assume the theorem holds for $2N - 8$. Then $r(2N) \leq r(2N - 8) + r(8) \leq (N - 3) + 4 = N + 1$, completing the induction (combined with the base cases $N = 8, 9, 10, 11$ above).

nodes.name: Theorem II (improved upper bound)
nodes.statement: For every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $N_0(\epsilon)$ such that for all $N > N_0(\epsilon)$: $r(N) < (\tfrac{1}{2} + \epsilon) N$.
nodes.statement_clean: For sufficiently large $N$, the density of any 3-AP-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is strictly less than $\tfrac{1}{2}$.
nodes.notes: The displayed bound was garbled in PDF→text extraction; reconstructed from the statement r(N) < (1/2+ε)N appearing later in the proof. Best-effort reading.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem II
nodes.statement: Show $r(17) = 8$ via case analysis using $r(14) = 8$, deduce $r(34) \leq 16$ and $r(35) \leq 16$. By induction, $r(71) \leq 32, \ldots, r(2^k + 2^{k-1} - 1) \leq 2^{k-1}$. A longer extension yields $r(18) = r(19) = r(20) = 8$ and $r(21) = r(22) = r(23) = 9$, giving $r(N) < (\tfrac{1}{2} + \epsilon) N$ for large $N$.
nodes.statement_clean: Case analysis at small $N$ followed by doubling-style induction.

nodes.name: Show $r(17) = 8$
nodes.statement: Since $r(14) = 8$, $r(17) \geq 8$. If $r(17) = 9$, then $1$ and $17$ must occur (else $r(17) \leq r(14) = 8$), forbidding $9$; then by translation $r(17) \leq r(8) + r(8) = 8$, contradiction. Hence $r(17) = 8$.

nodes.name: Bound $r(34) \leq 16$ and $r(35) \leq 16$
nodes.statement: From $r(17) = 8$, subadditivity gives $r(34) \leq 16$. If $r(35) \geq 17$, then by $r(34) \leq 16$, both $1$ and $35$ lie in the sequence, but then $18$ is forbidden (else $1, 18, 35$ form an AP), so $r(35) \leq 16$ by the same argument.

nodes.name: Doubling induction
nodes.statement: Iterating: $r(71) \leq 32, \ldots, r(2^k + 2^{k-1} - 1) \leq 2^{k-1}$, yielding the asymptotic density bound.

nodes.name: Sharpen via $r(20), r(21), r(22), r(23)$
nodes.statement: A longer but similar argument shows $r(18) = r(19) = r(20) = 8$ and $r(21) = r(22) = r(23) = 9$ (witnessed e.g. by $\{1, 3, 4, 8, 9, 16, 18, 19, 21\}$ for $r(21) = 9$). These yield $r(N) < (\tfrac{1}{2} + \epsilon) N$ for $N > N(\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Witness for $r(41) = 16$
nodes.statement: The sequence $1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 11, 13, 14, 28, 29, 31, 32, 37, 38, 40, 41$ is an A-sequence of length $16$ in $\{1,\ldots,41\}$, showing $r(41) = 16$ (combined with the bound $r(41) \leq 16$ derived from $r(20) = 8$).
nodes.statement_clean: An explicit 16-element 3-AP-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,41\}$.

nodes.name: Ternary-digit construction
nodes.statement: If $u < \tfrac{1}{2}(3^k + 1)$ is any integer not containing the digit $2$ in its ternary expansion, then the integers $u + 1$ form an A-sequence; hence $r\{\tfrac{1}{2}(3^k + 1)\} \geq 2^k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Integers with only digits $0, 1$ in base 3 form a 3-AP-free set of size $2^k$ in $\{1,\ldots,\tfrac{1}{2}(3^k+1)\}$.

nodes.name: Szekeres conjecture (3-AP)
nodes.statement_clean: Szekeres conjectured that the ternary-digit construction is optimal: $r(\tfrac{1}{2}(3^k+1)) = 2^k$.

nodes.name: Szekeres conjecture (general $l$)
nodes.statement: For any prime $p$ and any $\epsilon$: $r_p\!\left(\tfrac{p^k - 1}{p - 1}\right) = (p - 1)^k$ (best-effort reading; the displayed formula is partially garbled in PDF→text).
nodes.statement_clean: Generalized Szekeres conjecture for $l$-AP-free sets, parameterized by a prime $p$.
nodes.notes: The PDF→text rendering of the formula is partially corrupted; symbol layout reconstructed conservatively.

nodes.name: Primes in arithmetic progression (consequence of Szekeres)
nodes.statement: If the Szekeres conjecture (CnjP340.2) holds, then for every $k$ there are infinitely many $k$-term arithmetic progressions of primes.
nodes.statement_clean: Conditional on the Szekeres conjecture: infinitely many $k$-APs of primes for every $k$.

nodes.name: Improved van der Waerden bound (consequence of Szekeres)
nodes.statement: If the Szekeres conjecture (CnjP340.2) holds, then $f(k, l) < l^{e^{k \log k}}$ (best-effort reading: the displayed bound has the form $f(k,l) < l \cdot e^{k \log k}$ or similar; PDF→text rendering is garbled).
nodes.statement_clean: Conditional improvement on van der Waerden's quantitative bound.
nodes.notes: The displayed bound in the PDF→text was hard to read; reconstructed as best-effort. The original gives an exponential-type upper bound on $f(k,l)$.

nodes.name: Conjecture: $r(N) = o(N)$
nodes.statement: It is probable that $r(N) = o(N)$, i.e., the maximum size of a 3-AP-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has density tending to $0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Conjecture that 3-AP-free sets have density tending to zero.

nodes.name: van der Waerden's theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: For every $k, l$, there exists $N = f(k, l)$ such that any $l$-coloring of $\{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical van der Waerden theorem invoked as background.
